# YSS236 (VOP3-1) microcode, FS1R v1.20 EPROM

Generated by `tools/extract_vop3.py`. **Reference material only.** The filter and the effects the
emulator ships are models, because nobody has decoded this instruction set. The YSS236 is Yamaha's
VOP3, the same programmable DSP that is the synthesis engine of the AN1x, the AN200 and the
PLG150-AN and the vocal harmony processor of the PSR-9000, so a decode would reach well past this
one machine. No public description of the encoding exists.

**This is VOP3-1's program, the per-voice filter, not the effects.** The FS1R has two VOP3s with a
register window each on CS2, decoded on A8 and A9: VOP3-1 at 0x800200 and VOP3-2 at 0x800000
(`docs/research.md` section 8). The upload below is the 0x800200 one. VOP3-2's effect microcode is
the pair of images at EPROM 0x372204 and 0x373604 that `FUN_0003C9C4` uploads through
`FUN_00039648`, and it has not been extracted.

The chip's pinout is in `docs/vop3_pinout.md`, out of the AN200 service manual: 128 CPU registers,
8 serial audio inputs and 8 outputs, and a bank of external DRAM per chip. IC31, the FS1R's VOP3-1,
has nothing on those memory pins, which is why it cannot be the chip running the reverb.

## Bus and boot sequence (FUN_0000BC8C)

`FUN_0000B5E2(reg, value)` writes `0x800200 + reg * 2`, a 16-bit register block; status is at
0x800242. Register 0 selects an address, bit 15 of it selecting a second address space. The boot
upload runs in this order:

| step | register | source | count |
|---|---|---|---|
| reset | 1 | - | - |
| mode | 5 | constant 0x1004 | - |
| per-bus levels | 0x16 (address = bus + 1 in reg 0) | 0x37861A | 15 bytes |
| per-bus | 0x28 | constant 0x15 | 15 |
| per-bus | 0x29 | constant 0x15 | 15 |
| per-bus | 0x2A | constant 0 | 15 |
| per-bus | (image 0x1000) | constant 0x1000 | 15 words |
| byte table | 0xC, address from 0x37501A \| 0x8000 | 0x375C1A | 512 bytes |
| program | 10, 9, 8, 7, 6 per step | 0x375E1A (alt 0x37721A) | 512 x 5 words |
| coefficients | 0xB, address from 0x37501A | 0x37541A (alt 0x37581A) | 512 words |
| finish | 0x16 address 0, value 0x17; then 0x17 = 0 | - | - |

The boot argument picks one of two variants, and it is a literal at both call sites: FUN_0000B010
passes 0 on the normal boot, FUN_0000B0E2 passes 1 from FUN_003C2038, the diagnostic entry. So the
two are the ordinary and the test configuration of one chip, not one program per chip.

A filter type change (FUN_0000D050) does not re-upload: it mutes the channel's block, patches
program steps through FUN_0000B600 from a table indexed by type, and unmutes.

## Filter channel to program block (0x374F2E)

One byte per filter channel, 0 to 15, naming the program block FUN_0000D050 patches. It is a
rotation, channel n to block n + 2, which is what identified this block as the filter's:

```
00: 02 03 04 05 06 07 08 09 0A 0B 0C 0D 0E 0F 00 01
```

## Per-type patch table (0x378629)

```
01 02 03 21 35 36 04 05 06 22 39 3A 07 08 09 23 3D 3E 0A
```

## Per-bus levels (0x37861A, register 0x16)

```
17 12 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 0B 40
```
